audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Judges / Shoftim Song of Deborah war poem, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for archaic Hebrew poetry, YHWH theophany, Deborah's rise as mother in Israel, tribal participation and nonparticipation, Kishon battle imagery, Meroz curse, Jael blessing and killing, Sisera's mother scene, and forty-year quiet.

verses.restored: Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang on that day, saying:

familiar.text: Then sang Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam on that day, saying,

modern.text: On that day Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang this song:

original.text: וַתָּ֣שַׁר דְּבוֹרָ֔ה וּבָרָ֖ק בֶּן אֲבִינֹ֑עַם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: When locks were loosed/leaders led in Israel, when people freely offered themselves, bless YHWH.

familiar.text: Praise ye the LORD for the avenging of Israel, when the people willingly offered themselves.

modern.text: “When the princes take the lead in Israel, when the people volunteer, bless the LORD.

original.text: בִּפְרֹ֤עַ פְּרָעוֹת֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּהִתְנַדֵּ֖ב עָ֑ם בָּרֲכ֖וּ יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Hear, kings; give ear, rulers. I, to YHWH, I will sing; I will make melody to YHWH, Divine of Israel.

familiar.text: Hear, O ye kings; give ear, O ye princes; I, even I, will sing unto the LORD; I will sing praise to the LORD God of Israel.

modern.text: Listen, O kings! Give ear, O princes! I will sing to the LORD; I will sing praise to the LORD, the God of Israel.

original.text: שִׁמְע֣וּ מְלָכִ֔ים הַאֲזִ֖ינוּ רֹֽזְנִ֑ים אָֽנֹכִ֗י לַֽיהוָה֙ אָנֹכִ֣י אָשִׁ֔ירָה אֲזַמֵּ֕ר לַֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: YHWH, when you went out from Seir, when you marched from field of Edom, earth quaked, heavens also dripped, clouds also dripped water.

familiar.text: LORD, when thou wentest out of Seir, when thou marchedst out of the field of Edom, the earth trembled, and the heavens dropped, the clouds also dropped water.

modern.text: O LORD, when You went out from Seir, when You marched from the land of Edom, the earth trembled, the heavens poured out rain, and the clouds poured down water.

original.text: יְהוָ֗ה בְּצֵאתְךָ֤ מִשֵּׂעִיר֙ בְּצַעְדְּךָ֙ מִשְּׂדֵ֣ה אֱד֔וֹם אֶ֣רֶץ רָעָ֔שָׁה גַּם שָׁמַ֖יִם נָטָ֑פוּ גַּם עָבִ֖ים נָ֥טְפוּ מָֽיִם

verses.restored: Mountains flowed before YHWH, this Sinai, before YHWH, Divine of Israel.

familiar.text: The mountains melted from before the LORD, even that Sinai from before the LORD God of Israel.

modern.text: The mountains quaked before the LORD, the One of Sinai, before the LORD, the God of Israel.

original.text: הָרִ֥ים נָזְל֖וּ מִפְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה זֶ֣ה סִינַ֔י מִפְּנֵ֕י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: In days of Shamgar son of Anath, in days of Jael, roads ceased, and walkers of paths went by crooked roads.

familiar.text: In the days of Shamgar the son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were unoccupied, and the travellers walked through byways.

modern.text: In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were deserted and the travelers took the byways.

original.text: בִּימֵ֞י שַׁמְגַּ֤ר בֶּן עֲנָת֙ בִּימֵ֣י יָעֵ֔ל חָדְל֖וּ אֳרָח֑וֹת וְהֹלְכֵ֣י נְתִיב֔וֹת יֵלְכ֕וּ אֳרָח֖וֹת עֲקַלְקַלּֽוֹת

verses.restored: Villages/warriors ceased in Israel, they ceased, until I, Deborah, arose; I arose as mother in Israel.

familiar.text: The inhabitants of the villages ceased, they ceased in Israel, until that I Deborah arose, that I arose a mother in Israel.

modern.text: Life in the villages ceased; it ended in Israel, until I, Deborah, arose, a mother in Israel.

original.text: חָדְל֧וּ פְרָז֛וֹן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל חָדֵ֑לּוּ עַ֤ד שַׁקַּ֨מְתִּי֙ דְּבוֹרָ֔ה שַׁקַּ֥מְתִּי אֵ֖ם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: They chose new gods; then war was in gates. Was shield or spear seen among forty thousand in Israel?

familiar.text: They chose new gods; then was war in the gates: was there a shield or spear seen among forty thousand in Israel?

modern.text: When they chose new gods, then war came to their gates. Not a shield or spear was found among forty thousand in Israel.

original.text: יִבְחַר֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים חֲדָשִׁ֔ים אָ֖ז לָחֶ֣ם שְׁעָרִ֑ים מָגֵ֤ן אִם יֵֽרָאֶה֙ וָרֹ֔מַח בְּאַרְבָּעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: My heart is toward commanders of Israel, those freely offering themselves among people. Bless YHWH.

familiar.text: My heart is toward the governors of Israel, that offered themselves willingly among the people. Bless ye the LORD.

modern.text: My heart is with the princes of Israel, with the volunteers among the people. Bless the LORD!

original.text: לִבִּי֙ לְחוֹקְקֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַמִּֽתְנַדְּבִ֖ים בָּעָ֑ם בָּרֲכ֖וּ יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Riders on white/dappled donkeys, sitters on carpets, and walkers on way, speak.

familiar.text: Speak, ye that ride on white asses, ye that sit in judgment, and walk by the way.

modern.text: You who ride white donkeys, who sit on saddle blankets, and you who travel the road, ponder

original.text: רֹכְבֵי֩ אֲתֹנ֨וֹת צְחֹר֜וֹת יֹשְׁבֵ֧י עַל מִדִּ֛ין וְהֹלְכֵ֥י עַל דֶּ֖רֶךְ שִֽׂיחוּ

verses.restored: From sound of those dividing at watering places, there they recount righteous acts of YHWH, righteous acts of his villages/warriors in Israel. Then people of YHWH went down to gates.

familiar.text: They that are delivered from the noise of archers in the places of drawing water, there shall they rehearse the righteous acts of the LORD, even the righteous acts toward the inhabitants of his villages in Israel: then shall the people of the LORD go down to the gates.

modern.text: the voices of the singers at the watering places. There they shall recount the righteous acts of the LORD, the righteous deeds of His villagers in Israel. Then the people of the LORD went down to the gates:

original.text: מִקּ֣וֹל מְחַֽצְצִ֗ים בֵּ֚ין מַשְׁאַבִּ֔ים שָׁ֤ם יְתַנּוּ֙ צִדְק֣וֹת יְהוָ֔ה צִדְקֹ֥ת פִּרְזֹנ֖וֹ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אָ֛ז יָרְד֥וּ לַשְּׁעָרִ֖ים עַם יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Awake, awake, Deborah! Awake, awake, speak a song! Rise, Barak, and take captive your captives, son of Abinoam!

familiar.text: Awake, awake, Deborah: awake, awake, utter a song: arise, Barak, and lead thy captivity captive, thou son of Abinoam.

modern.text: ‘Awake, awake, O Deborah! Awake, awake, sing a song! Arise, O Barak, and take hold of your captives, O son of Abinoam!’

original.text: עוּרִ֤י עוּרִי֙ דְּבוֹרָ֔ה ע֥וּרִי ע֖וּרִי דַּבְּרִי שִׁ֑יר ק֥וּם בָּרָ֛ק וּֽשֲׁבֵ֥ה שֶׁבְיְךָ֖ בֶּן אֲבִינֹֽעַם

verses.restored: Then remnant came down to nobles; people of YHWH came down for me against mighty ones.

familiar.text: Then he made him that remaineth have dominion over the nobles among the people: the LORD made me have dominion over the mighty.

modern.text: Then the survivors came down to the nobles; the people of the LORD came down to me against the mighty.

original.text: אָ֚ז יְרַ֣ד שָׂרִ֔יד לְאַדִּירִ֖ים עָ֑ם יְהוָ֕ה יְרַד לִ֖י בַּגִּבּוֹרִֽים

verses.restored: From Ephraim their root was in Amalek; after you, Benjamin, among your peoples. From Machir commanders came down, and from Zebulun those bearing staff of scribe.

familiar.text: Out of Ephraim was there a root of them against Amalek; after thee, Benjamin, among thy people; out of Machir came down governors, and out of Zebulun they that handle the pen of the writer.

modern.text: Some came from Ephraim, with their roots in Amalek; Benjamin came with your people after you. The commanders came down from Machir, the bearers of the marshal’s staff from Zebulun.

original.text: מִנִּ֣י אֶפְרַ֗יִם שָׁרְשָׁם֙ בַּעֲמָלֵ֔ק אַחֲרֶ֥יךָ בִנְיָמִ֖ין בַּֽעֲמָמֶ֑יךָ מִנִּ֣י מָכִ֗יר יָֽרְדוּ֙ מְחֹ֣קְקִ֔ים וּמִ֨זְּבוּלֻ֔ן מֹשְׁכִ֖ים בְּשֵׁ֥בֶט סֹפֵֽר

verses.restored: Princes in Issachar were with Deborah; Issachar was so with Barak, sent into valley at his feet. Among divisions of Reuben were great resolves of heart.

familiar.text: And the princes of Issachar were with Deborah; even Issachar, and also Barak: he was sent on foot into the valley. For the divisions of Reuben there were great thoughts of heart.

modern.text: The princes of Issachar were with Deborah, and Issachar was with Barak, rushing into the valley at his heels. In the clans of Reuben there was great indecision.

original.text: וְשָׂרַ֤י בְּיִשָּׂשכָר֙ עִם דְּבֹרָ֔ה וְיִשָּׂשכָר֙ כֵּ֣ן בָּרָ֔ק בָּעֵ֖מֶק שֻׁלַּ֣ח בְּרַגְלָ֑יו בִּפְלַגּ֣וֹת רְאוּבֵ֔ן גְּדֹלִ֖ים חִקְקֵי לֵֽב

verses.restored: Why did you sit among sheepfolds, to hear piping for flocks? Among divisions of Reuben were great searchings of heart.

familiar.text: Why abodest thou among the sheepfolds, to hear the bleatings of the flocks? For the divisions of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.

modern.text: Why did you sit among the sheepfolds to hear the whistling for the flocks? In the clans of Reuben there was great indecision.

original.text: לָ֣מָּה יָשַׁ֗בְתָּ בֵּ֚ין הַֽמִּשְׁפְּתַ֔יִם לִשְׁמֹ֖עַ שְׁרִק֣וֹת עֲדָרִ֑ים לִפְלַגּ֣וֹת רְאוּבֵ֔ן גְּדוֹלִ֖ים חִקְרֵי לֵֽב

verses.restored: Gilead stayed across Jordan; Dan, why did he sojourn by ships? Asher sat by shore of seas and stayed by his landings.

familiar.text: Gilead abode beyond Jordan: and why did Dan remain in ships? Asher continued on the sea shore, and abode in his breaches.

modern.text: Gilead remained beyond the Jordan. Dan, why did you linger by the ships? Asher stayed at the coast and remained in his harbors.

original.text: גִּלְעָ֗ד בְּעֵ֤בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ שָׁכֵ֔ן וְדָ֕ן לָ֥מָּה יָג֖וּר אֳנִיּ֑וֹת אָשֵׁ֗ר יָשַׁב֙ לְח֣וֹף יַמִּ֔ים וְעַ֥ל מִפְרָצָ֖יו יִשְׁכּֽוֹן

verses.restored: Zebulun was a people that scorned its soul/life to death, and Naphtali, upon heights of field.

familiar.text: Zebulun and Naphtali were a people that jeoparded their lives unto the death in the high places of the field.

modern.text: Zebulun was a people who risked their lives; Naphtali, too, on the heights of the battlefield.

original.text: זְבֻל֗וּן עַ֣ם חֵרֵ֥ף נַפְשׁ֛וֹ לָמ֖וּת וְנַפְתָּלִ֑י עַ֖ל מְרוֹמֵ֥י שָׂדֶֽה

verses.restored: Kings came, they fought; then kings of Canaan fought at Taanach by waters of Megiddo. Gain of silver they did not take.

familiar.text: The kings came and fought, then fought the kings of Canaan in Taanach by the waters of Megiddo; they took no gain of money.

modern.text: Kings came and fought; then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo, but they took no plunder of silver.

original.text: בָּ֤אוּ מְלָכִים֙ נִלְחָ֔מוּ אָ֤ז נִלְחֲמוּ֙ מַלְכֵ֣י כְנַ֔עַן בְּתַעְנַ֖ךְ עַל מֵ֣י מְגִדּ֑וֹ בֶּ֥צַע כֶּ֖סֶף לֹ֥א לָקָֽחוּ

verses.restored: From heavens stars fought; from their courses they fought against Sisera.

familiar.text: They fought from heaven; the stars in their courses fought against Sisera.

modern.text: From the heavens the stars fought; from their courses they fought against Sisera.

original.text: מִן שָׁמַ֖יִם נִלְחָ֑מוּ הַכּֽוֹכָבִים֙ מִמְּסִלּוֹתָ֔ם נִלְחֲמ֖וּ עִם סִיסְרָֽא

verses.restored: Wadi Kishon swept them away, ancient wadi, wadi Kishon. March on, my soul/life, with strength.

familiar.text: The river of Kishon swept them away, that ancient river, the river Kishon. O my soul, thou hast trodden down strength.

modern.text: The River Kishon swept them away, the ancient river, the River Kishon. March on, O my soul, in strength!

original.text: נַ֤חַל קִישׁוֹן֙ גְּרָפָ֔ם נַ֥חַל קְדוּמִ֖ים נַ֣חַל קִישׁ֑וֹן תִּדְרְכִ֥י נַפְשִׁ֖י עֹֽז

verses.restored: Then horse hooves hammered from galloping, galloping of his mighty ones.

familiar.text: Then were the horsehoofs broken by the means of the pransings, the pransings of their mighty ones.

modern.text: Then the hooves of horses thundered— the mad galloping of his stallions.

original.text: אָ֥ז הָלְמ֖וּ עִקְּבֵי ס֑וּס מִֽדַּהֲר֖וֹת דַּהֲר֥וֹת אַבִּירָֽיו

verses.restored: Curse Meroz, said messenger of YHWH; curse, curse its inhabitants, because they did not come to help YHWH, to help YHWH against mighty ones.

familiar.text: Curse ye Meroz, said the angel of the LORD, curse ye bitterly the inhabitants thereof; because they came not to the help of the LORD, to the help of the LORD against the mighty.

modern.text: ‘Curse Meroz,’ says the angel of the LORD. ‘Bitterly curse her inhabitants; for they did not come to help the LORD, to help the LORD against the mighty.’

original.text: א֣וֹרוּ מֵר֗וֹז אָמַר֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה אֹ֥רוּ אָר֖וֹר יֹשְׁבֶ֑יהָ כִּ֤י לֹֽא בָ֨אוּ֙ לְעֶזְרַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה לְעֶזְרַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה בַּגִּבּוֹרִֽים

verses.restored: Most blessed of women is Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite; above women in tent she is blessed.

familiar.text: Blessed above women shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be, blessed shall she be above women in the tent.

modern.text: Most blessed among women is Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, most blessed of tent-dwelling women.

original.text: תְּבֹרַךְ֙ מִנָּשִׁ֔ים יָעֵ֕ל אֵ֖שֶׁת חֶ֣בֶר הַקֵּינִ֑י מִנָּשִׁ֥ים בָּאֹ֖הֶל תְּבֹרָֽךְ

verses.restored: Water he asked; milk she gave. In a bowl of nobles she brought curds.

familiar.text: He asked water, and she gave him milk; she brought forth butter in a lordly dish.

modern.text: He asked for water, and she gave him milk. In a magnificent bowl she brought him curds.

original.text: מַ֥יִם שָׁאַ֖ל חָלָ֣ב נָתָ֑נָה בְּסֵ֥פֶל אַדִּירִ֖ים הִקְרִ֥יבָה חֶמְאָֽה

verses.restored: Her hand she sent to tent peg, and her right hand to workman's hammer. She hammered Sisera, crushed his head, shattered and pierced his temple.

familiar.text: She put her hand to the nail, and her right hand to the workmen’s hammer; and with the hammer she smote Sisera, she smote off his head, when she had pierced and stricken through his temples.

modern.text: She reached for the tent peg, her right hand for the workman’s hammer. She struck Sisera and crushed his skull; she shattered and pierced his temple.

original.text: יָדָהּ֙ לַיָּתֵ֣ד תִּשְׁלַ֔חְנָה וִֽימִינָ֖הּ לְהַלְמ֣וּת עֲמֵלִ֑ים וְהָלְמָ֤ה סִֽיסְרָא֙ מָחֲקָ֣ה רֹאשׁ֔וֹ וּמָחֲצָ֥ה וְחָלְפָ֖ה רַקָּתֽוֹ

verses.restored: Between her feet he bowed, fell, lay; between her feet he bowed, fell. Where he bowed, there he fell, destroyed.

familiar.text: At her feet he bowed, he fell, he lay down: at her feet he bowed, he fell: where he bowed, there he fell down dead.

modern.text: At her feet he collapsed, he fell, there he lay still; at her feet he collapsed, he fell; where he collapsed, there he fell dead.

original.text: בֵּ֣ין רַגְלֶ֔יהָ כָּרַ֥ע נָפַ֖ל שָׁכָ֑ב בֵּ֤ין רַגְלֶ֨יהָ֙ כָּרַ֣ע נָפָ֔ל בַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּרַ֔ע שָׁ֖ם נָפַ֥ל שָׁדֽוּד

verses.restored: Through window she looked out and cried, mother of Sisera through lattice: Why is his chariot delayed in coming? Why are hoofbeats of his chariots late?

familiar.text: The mother of Sisera looked out at a window, and cried through the lattice, Why is his chariot so long in coming? why tarry the wheels of his chariots?

modern.text: Sisera’s mother looked through the window; she peered through the lattice and lamented: ‘Why is his chariot so long in coming? What has delayed the clatter of his chariots?’

original.text: בְּעַד֩ הַחַלּ֨וֹן נִשְׁקְפָ֧ה וַתְּיַבֵּ֛ב אֵ֥ם סִֽיסְרָ֖א בְּעַ֣ד הָֽאֶשְׁנָ֑ב מַדּ֗וּעַ בֹּשֵׁ֤שׁ רִכְבּוֹ֙ לָב֔וֹא מַדּ֣וּעַ אֶֽחֱר֔וּ פַּעֲמֵ֖י מַרְכְּבוֹתָֽיו

verses.restored: Wise princesses answered her; indeed she returned answer to herself:

familiar.text: Her wise ladies answered her, yea, she returned answer to herself,

modern.text: Her wisest ladies answer; indeed she keeps telling herself,

original.text: חַכְמ֥וֹת שָׂרוֹתֶ֖יהָ תַּעֲנֶ֑ינָּה אַף הִ֕יא תָּשִׁ֥יב אֲמָרֶ֖יהָ לָֽהּ

verses.restored: Are they not finding and dividing spoil? A womb, two wombs for every man; spoil of dyed garments for Sisera, spoil of dyed embroidered garments, dyed double-embroidered garments for necks of spoil.

familiar.text: Have they not sped? have they not divided the prey; to every man a damsel or two; to Sisera a prey of divers colours, a prey of divers colours of needlework, of divers colours of needlework on both sides, meet for the necks of them that take the spoil?

modern.text: ‘Are they not finding and dividing the spoil— a girl or two for each warrior, a plunder of dyed garments for Sisera, the spoil of embroidered garments for the neck of the looter?’

verses.restored: So may all your enemies perish, YHWH; but those loving him be like sun going out in its might. And land was quiet forty years.

familiar.text: So let all thine enemies perish, O LORD: but let them that love him be as the sun when he goeth forth in his might. And the land had rest forty years.

modern.text: So may all your enemies perish, O LORD! But may those who love You shine like the sun at its brightest.” And the land had rest for forty years.

translation_notes: Judges 5 is among the oldest and most difficult Hebrew poems in the Bible; many lines contain rare vocabulary, compressed syntax, and debated tribal/geographic references.
The opening blessing may refer to loosened hair or leaders leading; both fit scenes of voluntary mobilization and require philological audit.
Deborah's self-description as 'mother in Israel' is public leadership imagery, not a reduction of women to biological motherhood.

The poem praises tribes that joined and critiques those that did not. It must not become a modern template for shaming civilians, conscientious objectors, disabled people, caregivers, or noncombatants for not entering war.
Stars fighting and Kishon sweeping away enemies are cosmic war-poetry images, not astronomical claims or weather prooftexts.
The curse of Meroz is war-poetry rhetoric and must not authorize cursing, violence, or communal punishment against people who refuse militarized participation.
Jael's blessing is poetic celebration of a killing. Her agency and the end of Sisera's violence are visible, but the act remains graphic and non-generalizable.

Sisera's mother's scene is bitter irony: she imagines rape and plunder as the reason for delay. The line exposes war's sexual violence without endorsing it; the phrase 'womb, two wombs' is deliberately dehumanizing and must not be softened into harmless spoil.
safety_note: Do not use Judges 5 to glorify war, shame noncombatants, curse communities, promote sexual violence, mock grieving mothers, or turn Jael's killing into a general model. Preserve Deborah's leadership, voluntary courage, and the poem's exposure of war brutality while keeping its violent triumphalism under moral restraint.
